def: The process by which a cell engulfs material by pinching in its membrane to form a vesicle. In the thyroid, follicular cells endocytose thyroglobulin to release T3 and T4.

Waxy, non-pitting thickening of the skin over the shins in Graves disease, from glycosaminoglycan deposition driven by TSH receptor antibodies. The term "pretibial" simply means in front of the tibia (shin).
An intermediate in cortisol synthesis made from 17-hydroxyprogesterone by 21-hydroxylase and converted to cortisol by 11-beta-hydroxylase. It builds up in 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency.
Conversion of androgens (testosterone, androstenedione) into estrogens by the enzyme aromatase, which occurs in ovarian granulosa cells, placenta and fat.
The four small glands behind the thyroid that secrete parathyroid hormone to raise blood calcium.
A benign inherited condition from inactivating mutations of the calcium-sensing receptor, causing high blood calcium with unusually low urinary calcium excretion.
The medical specialty of ear, nose and throat disorders (ENT).
Relating to meiosis, the cell division producing haploid gametes. Oocytes arrest in prophase I until ovulation.
The embryonic duct (Müllerian duct) that forms the fallopian tubes, uterus and upper vagina. It regresses in males under anti-Müllerian hormone.
The onset of breast development at puberty, with breast bud formation; Tanner stage II.
Elevation of the testis when the inner thigh is stroked, mediated by the genitofemoral nerve. It is absent in testicular torsion.
Having two separate amniotic sacs. Twins that are diamniotic can be dichorionic or monochorionic.
A usually benign but locally aggressive tumor at the epiphysis of long bones near the knee, showing multinucleated giant cells on biopsy. Treated with denosumab.
DNA elements that bind transcription factors to boost transcription of a gene and can act at a distance from it, upstream, downstream or in introns.
A chromosome deletion too small to see on karyotype, found with FISH or microarray. Examples include DiGeorge (22q11) and Prader-Willi syndromes.
Located within the marrow cavity of a bone, as in intramedullary rods or tumors; also means inside the spinal cord.
Fusion of the long arms of two acrocentric chromosomes (13, 14, 15, 21, 22) with loss of the short arms. A cause of familial Down syndrome.
Describing iron in the Fe2+ state, the form that binds oxygen in hemoglobin. Oxidation to ferric (Fe3+) gives methemoglobin.
Consolidation of lung tissue in lobar pneumonia, making it firm and liver-like as alveoli fill with exudate. Stages are red then gray hepatization.
A hypersensitivity pneumonitis from moldy cork dust.
An aromatic amine in dyes and cigarette smoke, a carcinogen linked to bladder cancer.
Elevation of liver enzymes (AST and ALT) in the blood, indicating liver cell injury.
The point where the renal pelvis joins the ureter. Obstruction here is a common cause of hydronephrosis in children.
An antimuscarinic (M3 blocker) used for urgency incontinence and overactive bladder. Causes dry mouth, constipation and urinary retention.
Absence of a functioning spleen, leading to Howell-Jolly bodies and risk of infection by encapsulated organisms.
Relating to helminths, parasitic worms such as roundworms, tapeworms and flukes.
The embryonic gut portion giving rise to the distal third of the transverse colon through the rectum, supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery.
The main tongue protrusion muscle, innervated by CN XII. Weakness makes the tongue deviate toward the weak side.
The only tongue muscle innervated by the vagus nerve (CN X) instead of CN XII.
The cerebellar lobe that connects with vestibular nuclei to control balance and eye movements. Lesions cause truncal ataxia and nystagmus.
Occurring outside lymph nodes, as in lymphomas arising in the gut, brain or skin.
The junction between the sigmoid colon and rectum.
The space behind the peritoneal cavity containing kidneys, adrenals, pancreas, aorta and parts of the duodenum and colon.
The point where the common bile duct and pancreatic duct join and empty into the duodenum. "Ampullary" describes it.
A dopaminergic pathway from the ventral tegmental area to the nucleus accumbens and limbic system, linked to reward. Overactivity is linked to positive symptoms of schizophrenia.
The dopaminergic pathway from the substantia nigra to the striatum that controls movement. Degenerates in Parkinson disease.
The part of the lesser omentum from the liver to the duodenum, containing the portal triad (hepatic artery, portal vein, bile duct). Compressed in the Pringle maneuver.
Trapping of a herniated bowel segment so it cannot be pushed back (irreducible), risking strangulation.
A finger or toe joint. Heberden nodes affect the distal joints in osteoarthritis and Bouchard nodes affect the proximal ones.
Describing secretion in which the whole cell disintegrates to release its contents, as in sebaceous glands.
Resembling or related to urticaria (hives), with itchy raised wheals, as in allergic reactions.
The transverse carpal ligament that forms the roof of the carpal tunnel over the median nerve and flexor tendons.
